claim: THE STRESS-TIMING SPLIT (batch 47, pre-registration commit 982cb81): write-time vs read-time ionic stress on the commit machinery. Tazumi 2026 (APA): salt exposure disrupts memory RETRIEVAL in D. japonica while leaving storage intact — the timing split. The stack analog runs as-is on the commit-noise machinery: the ionic exposure IS the depolarized floor (exp169's disclosed -35.0 pin form), and the machinery has a clean write/read boundary — the WALK (the commits) is the storage face, the SETTLE+DECODE is the retrieval face. The 72-row substituted battery (exp256's, 12 hosts x 3 seeds x r-60i0/r-60i1 at n=400, the exp287/exp288 traced replica form at the production budget 8) runs under three floor states: A0 the -60.0 anchor (the S0 bit-exact form), A1 the -35.0 pin during the walk only (from the encode window's start through the last commit), A2 the -35.0 pin during the settle only.
